newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices steady on low arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices steady on low arrivals.

text.p: Indian cotton prices held steady on Thursday on low arrivals but at improved levels, dealers said.
Fresh physical buying however remained slow. Limited arrivals and reports of higher export of cotton yarn kept offerings at a low ebb.
Arrivals remained low due to a drop in supplies at producing centres as the end of the cotton season neared.

Daily arrivals of cotton in the Punjab region have fallen to 1,000/1,500 rupees bales (170 kg each). In spot deals Bengal-deshi was steady at 900/935 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned was quiet at 1,600/1,700 rupees per maund.
Medium-staple Gujarat Kalyan was quoted at the previous level of 13,700/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) so did long- staple Gujarat Sankar-4 at 17,000/20,000 rupees per candy.
